summary: Adds tenant-bound workload APIs for idempotently registering and decommissioning managed Operaton engines without exposing engine credentials.
userImpact: Managed Cloud orchestration can connect and safely decommission a provisioned Operaton engine through a host-owned, dedicated-tenant workload contract.

instructions: Cloud control-plane callers must adopt the workload-authenticated registration contract before invoking this endpoint.

configuration: Set EG_MANAGED_ENGINE_INTERNAL_DNS_SUFFIX to the exact managed Kubernetes service suffix; the existing private-host, insecure-HTTP, and engine-host allowlist opt-ins remain required.

changes: Adds workload-authenticated registration and decommission endpoints under /api/workloads/tenants/:tenantId with strict requests and signed, credential-free receipts.

notes: Implementation reuses existing TypeORM engine, external-registration, authorization, and lifecycle-ledger entities without a schema migration. The focused PostgreSQL persistence lifecycle passed; other supported databases remain a milestone acceptance gate.

security: Only tenant-lifecycle workload identity may register or decommission a managed engine; browser and general API authentication are rejected, and an absent receipt is signed only when no conflicting engine or registration exists.
Plaintext credentials are accepted only at the workload boundary for immediate literal AES-GCM encryption and are never returned or logged.
Only curated egme-<40 lowercase hex> Kubernetes service URLs under the configured suffix are accepted, and decommissioned engines are denied before outbound transport.
documentation: Updated the engine tenancy/provisioning API, pooled tenancy architecture, and configuration references with the workload lifecycle and endpoint boundary.
knownLimitations: Oracle, SQL Server, MySQL, and Spanner portability remain broader milestone acceptance gates; this change has focused PostgreSQL persistence evidence only.
A temporary Cloud stop retains the host registration; Cloud observed state must report stopped while host health polling reports the absent runtime unavailable.
rollback: Stop managed Cloud callers from invoking the additive endpoints before rolling back the host. Do not delete provider resources unless a signed host decommission receipt has already been verified; retained engine history remains safe.
validation: Focused unit and contract tests cover schemas, workload authorization, route inventory, idempotency, literal encryption, endpoint policy, runtime decommission denial, and signed absent decommission recovery.

PostgreSQL integration: 1 test passed for real TypeORM registration, exact replay, encrypted persistence, decommission, credential clearing, signed absence recovery, terminal recreation denial, and concurrent serialization.
